title: ERAN prototypes with WIDTH — does a shaped unit break the 74.24% ceiling?
hypothesis: A prototype is a POINT with an isotropic cosine. A real neuron's receptive field is a tuning curve with a WIDTH — it prefers a region, more strongly along some directions than others. ERAN already has a scalar version (Brain.tolerance = mean - k*sd of a unit's own absorbed similarities). This experiment makes that width PER-DIRECTION and asks whether it breaks the ceiling.

protocol.cochlea: eran-brain/body/ears.py EAR_REPR=cochlea, 8x24, dim 192, FROZEN; byte-identical snn-lab/cochlea.py
protocol.split: 396 train / 132 heldout, corpus-syllables — identical to the fair fight
protocol.dev: stratified + deterministic by sha1(filename), first 20% per class. 308 fit / 88 dev.
protocol.heldout_policy: opened once per arm, after every choice was fixed on dev
protocol.naming: each unit takes the class it won most often on TRAIN (proof/measure.py:fit_proto_labels); an unnamed unit scores WRONG
protocol.exposure: 30 passes over the training audio — inherited from the fair fight's dev choice, NOT re-tuned here
protocol.statistics: Wilson 95% intervals; exact two-sided McNemar on the same 132 items for every headline comparison

ARM2_diagonal_width__vs__ARM1_baseline_c.verdict: no significant difference at p<0.05 on any seed

ARM2_diagonal_width__vs__CONTROL_1nn.verdict: no significant difference at p<0.05 on any seed

ARM4_shared_whitening__vs__ARM1_baseline.verdict: no significant difference at p<0.05 on any seed

ARM4_shared_whitening__vs__CONTROL_1nn.verdict: no significant difference at p<0.05 on any seed

ARM4_shared_whitening__vs__CONTROL_neare.verdict: no significant difference at p<0.05 on any seed

ARM2b_online_width__vs__ARM1_baseline_co.verdict: no significant difference at p<0.05 on any seed

ARM2b_online_width__vs__CONTROL_1nn.verdict: no significant difference at p<0.05 on any seed

statistics.note: Exact two-sided McNemar on the same 132 heldout items, seed by seed. n10 = the arm was right where the reference was wrong; n01 = the reverse. Deterministic references (1-NN, centroid) are compared against each of the arm's three seeds.

ARM2_diagonal_width.cost_vs_baseline: 2x per unit (a mean AND a per-dimension variance)

ARM3_shrinkage_covariance.cost_vs_baseline: 98x per unit — a full covariance is 18528 numbers on top of a 192-number mean

ARM4_shared_whitening.cost_vs_baseline: 1x per unit + ONE shared 192x192 transform for the whole brain

CONTROL_nearest_class_centroid.note: uses LABELS to place its 22 units. That is why it is a control and not an arm.

budgets.budget_honesty: A width-carrying unit costs 2x a point unit; a full covariance costs ~97x. The shared whitening costs 1x per unit plus one 192x192 matrix for the entire brain. Any accuracy claim has to be read next to these numbers.

post_hoc_diagnostics._what_the_supervised_gaussian_tells_you: 22 class-conditional diagonal Gaussians, fitted with LABELS, on the same 396 training files. If per-direction width cannot beat the plain class centroid even when the grouping is perfect and every unit has 18 members, then width is not the missing ingredient for this ear on this task, and no unsupervised version of it can be.
post_hoc_diagnostics._why_occupancy_matters: A diagonal width needs 192 variances per unit. Seed 0's units hold 1 training sounds each (median). That is the whole reason the shrinkage has to be near 1, and the reason a per-unit width collapses onto the shared one.
post_hoc_diagnostics._read_this_as: POST HOC. The primary ARM 4 number (alpha 0.75, cov total, shrink 0.3) was chosen on dev before the exam. This curve is printed afterwards so the reader can see whether that number stood on a knife edge or on a plateau. It selects nothing.

mean_centering_only_heldout.note: identity transform + global mean removal + renormalise. This is the alpha=0 row of ARM 4's whitening curve, isolated. POST HOC on the 132 items; the clean evidence is the leave-one-session-out test.

supervised_diagonal_gaussian_vs_centroid.note: 22 class-conditional diagonal Gaussians vs 22 plain class means, both fitted WITH labels on the same 396 files. The decisive diagnostic: width works when the grouping is perfect.

secondary_protocol_session_grouped_dev._what_this_shows: Every arm re-tuned on a dev split that has the SAME structure as the real exam (a whole unseen recording session), instead of the primary harness's filename-hash split which leaves the same session on both sides. Compare the ordering here with dev_phase in the primary run.
secondary_protocol_session_grouped_dev._dev_gap: The primary dev split scores every arm roughly 14 points higher than the heldout does. That gap is session leakage, not overfitting to 88 items, and it is a property of the inherited harness, not of this experiment. Tomorrow's runs should use this session-grouped dev.

corpus_structure.note: 22 classes x 3 repeats per session. The heldout is two sessions never heard. The primary dev split is by sha1 of the filename, so it shares sessions with fit — measured as a ~14 point optimism.

confirmation_global_mean_removal._what_this_is: An INDEPENDENT confirmation of the one thing the width experiment actually found. Leave-one-session-out over the 6 training sessions; the 132-item heldout is never opened here. 6 folds x 3 seeds = 396 judgements, every one of them on a recording session the organism had not heard.
confirmation_global_mean_removal._the_change: Subtract the mean of every percept heard so far, then re-normalise to unit length, before the cosine. 192 shared numbers for the whole brain. No per-unit width of any kind.

protocol.mean_estimated_from: the 5 training sessions in each fold, never the held-out one

confirmation_global_mean_removal._honesty: The lead came from a POST-HOC row of the whitening curve (alpha=0 is the identity matrix, so that row was mean-centering all along) and the heldout number for it was already visible when we noticed. This leave-one-session-out test is the clean evidence: it uses only training data, 396 judgements, and a paired sign test across 18 independent runs. Read the 132-item heldout number for mean-centering (75.76%) as consistent with this, not as its proof.

verdict.one_line_en: NO. Giving a prototype per-direction width did not break the 74.24% prototype-family ceiling (best true width arm 72.73%, BELOW it), and nothing came near the 79.55% no-learning control. The only thing that moved was the cheap control, and inside that control the whole gain was global mean removal, not whitening.
verdict.one_line_he: לא. לתת לאב-טיפוס רוחב לכל כיוון לא שבר את תקרת 74.24% (הזרוע הכי טובה של רוחב אמיתי: 72.73%, מתחת לתקרה), ואף אחד לא התקרב לביקורת של 79.55% שלא לומדת כלום. הדבר היחיד שזז היה הביקורת הזולה — ובתוכה כל הרווח היה הורדת הממוצע הגלובלי, לא הלבנה.
verdict.why_the_auto_headline_says_yes: headline.broke_family_ceiling_7424 is computed mechanically over ALL arms including ARM 4, the cheap control. ARM 4 is not a width arm — it grows no shape on any unit. Its +2.02 points over the ceiling is 2.7 files out of 132 and McNemar gives p=0.50 on the pooled comparison. Read `verdict`, not `headline`.
what_redirects_tomorrow: The unit was NOT the ceiling. Per-direction width is the wrong knob for this ear on this task: the honest width arm landed 1.5 points BELOW the ceiling it was supposed to break, and the expensive version (full covariance) lost 9 points.

Width is starved, not wrong. With PERFECT groups and labels, 22 class-conditional diagonal Gaussians score 84.09% against 79.55% for the same 22 class means — width is worth +4.5 points when a unit has 18 members. Unsupervised units have a MEDIAN OF 1 member (108 of 184 units win exactly one training file). You cannot estimate 192 variances from one sample, and no regulariser rescues that.

The real lever found here is upstream of the unit: subtract the mean of everything heard, then renormalise. +5.72 points on leave-one-session-out (16 wins / 1 loss / 1 tie over 18 runs, sign test p=0.0003). 192 shared numbers for the whole brain, no per-unit state at all.
But it does not close the gap: mean removal lifts the controls too (centroid 80.81% -> 82.07%, 1-NN 78.28% -> 79.80% leave-one-session-out). The organism stays below the thing that does no learning.

The harness's dev split is session-contaminated and ~14 points optimistic: train is 6 sessions t00..t05, the heldout is 2 unseen sessions, but ff_lib.dev_mask splits by sha1 of the FILENAME so the same session sits on both sides. ARM 3 scored dev 88.64% and heldout 60.35% — a 28-point collapse, which is exactly what a per-unit covariance that memorises a session looks like. Future runs should use the leave-one-session-out dev in width_supp.py.
